detailed_description: The JSON Formatter formats or minifies pasted JSON in the browser. Paste JSON into the input textarea, click Format to parse it with JSON.parse and output two-space indented JSON, or click Minify to output compact JSON. If parsing fails, the page shows the browser JSON.parse error message. You can copy the generated output or clear both fields. The tool does not provide syntax highlighting, custom indentation controls, file upload, automatic JSON repair, schema validation, line-and-column diagnostics beyond the parser message, or large-file processing guarantees.
usage_steps: Paste JSON data into the input textarea.
Click Format to create a two-space indented JSON output.
Click Minify when you need compact JSON without extra whitespace.
Review any JSON.parse error message if the input is invalid.
Copy the output or use Clear to reset the fields.
usage_examples: Format a pasted API response before reading nested fields.
Minify a small JSON sample before adding it to a code snippet.
Check whether pasted JSON can be parsed by the browser.
Clear the input and output fields before testing another sample.

faqs.question: What happens if my JSON has a syntax error?
faqs.answer: The page shows the error message returned by JSON.parse and clears the output.

faqs.question: Does this tool support formatting JSON with custom indentation?
faqs.answer: No. The Format button outputs two-space indentation.

faqs.question: Can I format extremely large JSON files with this online tool?
faqs.answer: There is no special large-file mode. Very large pasted JSON may be slow or fail depending on your browser.

faqs.question: Is the JSON data I paste stored on your servers?
faqs.answer: No, all processing happens client-side in your browser. Your data is never sent to or stored on our servers.

faqs.question: Does the tool fix common JSON errors automatically?
faqs.answer: No. Invalid JSON must be corrected manually before it can be formatted or minified.
